compounding_issues: All 5 sessions aborted instantly with 'You've hit your session limit' (provider rate limit) — zero tokens/tool calls each, so no session ever produced work for a later session to build on
No retry/backoff or cascade recovery was triggered (cascade_recovery: false), so the provider rate limit compounded: every consecutive session stacked another empty commit with exit_code 1

The commits are empty stubs — only .instrument/session_N.jsonl error markers were committed; a naive git-log review would read the greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting messages as real progression when app.py is byte-identical to the seed

Seed/base mismatch: the tier2_small/good codebase is a Flask Auth API (~500 LOC), while the story prompts target a WebSocket notification server — no shared domain foundation between the base and the requested system
key_decisions: Designed a textbook incremental arc in the prompts: WebSocket server with per-client IDs (S1) → channel subscriptions (S2) → Redis pub/sub backbone (S3) → pluggable Transport interface for SSE/polling/raw TCP (S4) → Redis-counter rate limiting + persistent message history (S5)
Intended Redis-based architecture: pub/sub for fan-out and per-client-ID counters for rate limiting — a coherent distribution scheme for a notification service
Planned a pluggable transport abstraction (Session 4) positioned to refactor S1-S3 WebSocket-specific code — a sensible late refactor that would have depended on all prior sessions
None of these decisions were actually executed; the only real artifact is the decision to commit instrument markers even on total failure
